focus: Candidate (c) PreToolUse advisory, (d) no new surface, portability, cross-candidate comparison

statement: Candidate (c) shape: advisory naming rule file(s) for the matched action; spec-gate precedent proves the delivery machinery (tool sets, deliver-once, re-arm, kill switches); no tool-call-to-trigger-row mapping exists today — the classifier is the new work.

Candidate (c) silence: no row match + once-per-session delivery with boundary re-arm; cost: node process spawn per matched event + ~100-200B advisory; real frequency must be log-measured post-build (022 rule).
Candidate (c) matches on action — the router's own key; the only candidate addressing later-in-session actions; portable via shared core + per-runtime wiring; reads the per-repo router.
Candidate (d): no measured miss exists in the evidence base; status quo covers first write + replies; the flip test is a measured miss with cost.

Cross-candidate: only (c) is action-keyed; (a) fails 022's bar; (b) reverses a documented decision and is topic-keyed; (d) has no measured miss or win; (c) has the strongest precedent chain and its open risk is classifier quality.
No tool-call-to-trigger-row mapping module exists today; spec-gate classifies spec-folder intent, not rule rows.
All candidates respect 010's no-rule-growth constraint; emitted text must never embed the corpus path — router-relative only.
